sentences.en: An American story that we all know and that I've lived for a lot of my life is the story of rising incarceration.
sentences.zh: 我们都熟知且我亲身经历过的一段美国故事，就是监禁率不断上升的故事。

sentences.en: The United States prides itself on being a nation of freedom and liberty.
sentences.zh: 美国以身为自由之邦而自豪。

sentences.en: And yet, we have the biggest prison system in the history of the world.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们却拥有世界历史上规模最大的监狱系统。

sentences.en: And for many decades, that system was just growing and growing.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，这个系统一直在不断膨胀。

sentences.en: Including when it came to young people.
sentences.zh: 包括针对年轻人的部分。

sentences.en: But what if there was a disruption in that narrative?
sentences.zh: 但如果这种叙事被打破了呢？

sentences.en: What if the story changed?
sentences.zh: 如果故事发生了改变呢？

sentences.en: My name is James Forman Jr.
sentences.zh: 我叫小詹姆斯·福尔曼。

sentences.en: I'm a law professor at Yale University and a contributor to the New York Times Magazine.
sentences.zh: 我是耶鲁大学的法学教授，也是《纽约时报杂志》的撰稿人。

sentences.en: I became a public defender in the middle of this hyper-punitive era.
sentences.zh: 我是在这个极度惩罚性的时代成为公设辩护人的。

sentences.en: For six years, I represented young people in the juvenile and adult court systeMs.
sentences.zh: 六年来，我在少年和成人法庭系统中为年轻人辩护。

sentences.en: This was Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 那是华盛顿特区。

sentences.en: in the 1990s, when people were talking about locking up more of everybody.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪90年代，当时人们都在谈论要把更多的人关进监狱。

sentences.en: More young people were being charged as adults and even being sent to death row.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的年轻人被当作成年人起诉，甚至被送上死囚牢房。

sentences.en: As a defense lawyer, I was in the courtroom every day arguing for alternatives to prison for my clients.
sentences.zh: 作为一名辩护律师，我每天都在法庭上为我的当事人争取监狱以外的替代方案。

sentences.en: I would point to job training programs and mentoring programs, after-school tutoring and mental health treatment.
sentences.zh: 我会指出职业培训项目、指导项目、课后辅导和心理健康治疗等选择。

sentences.en: And the judge sitting across from me would often say things like,
sentences.zh: 而坐在我对面的法官通常会说这样的话：

sentences.en: Well, counselor, you know, I understand that your client has had a challenging life.
sentences.zh: “好吧，律师，我知道你的当事人生活坎坷。”

sentences.en: But part of what I have to do is send your client a message.
sentences.zh: “但我必须做的一部分工作是给你的当事人一个教训。”

sentences.en: So I'm going to give them a month or two months behind bars.
sentences.zh: “所以我打算判他们一个月或两个月的监禁。”

sentences.en: I could see that these judges were telling themselves a story, which was that a relatively short amount of time behind bars would be a wake-up call.
sentences.zh: 我看得出来，这些法官在给自己编造一个故事，认为相对短暂的监禁会起到警示作用。

sentences.en: In their mind, they were helping these kids.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，他们是在帮助这些孩子。

sentences.en: And even though I was sure they were wrong, I didn't really have the evidence to prove it.
sentences.zh: 尽管我确信他们错了，但我并没有真正的证据来证明这一点。

sentences.en: But then, this astonishing pattern started to emerge.
sentences.zh: 但随后，一个惊人的模式开始显现。

sentences.en: I remember getting an email two years ago from a non-profit called The Sentencing Project, which publishes data on youth incarceration.
sentences.zh: 我记得两年前收到了一封来自名为“量刑项目”的非营利组织的电子邮件，他们发布关于青少年监禁的数据。

sentences.en: And the graph I saw in their email was so stunning that I printed it out.
sentences.zh: 我在邮件中看到的图表太震撼了，我把它打印了出来。

sentences.en: And I literally, I wrote on the top,
sentences.zh: 我甚至在上面写道：

sentences.en: There's a story here right about this.
sentences.zh: “这里有一个关于这个的故事。”

sentences.en: This graph showed that we're locking up fewer young people than we did even in the 1970s when the era that we call mass incarceration really began.
sentences.zh: 这张图表显示，我们关押的年轻人比20世纪70年代还要少，而当时正是我们所称的“大规模监禁”时代的开端。

sentences.en: And what's so wild is that from 2000 to 2020, the number of young people behind bars dropped by 77%.
sentences.zh: 最疯狂的是，从2000年到2020年，身陷囹圄的年轻人数量下降了77%。

sentences.en: Picture a room, there's 100 people in the room, and then imagine that we take 77 of them out.
sentences.zh: 想象一个房间，里面有100个人，然后想象我们带走了其中的77个人。

sentences.en: So there's just 23 people left.
sentences.zh: 所以只剩下23个人了。

sentences.en: That's the decline.
sentences.zh: 这就是下降幅度。

sentences.en: And it's a massive change on its own.
sentences.zh: 这本身就是一个巨大的变化。

sentences.en: But if you say to someone,
sentences.zh: 但如果你对某人说：

sentences.en: Wow, we stopped locking up so many young people, their first reaction might be,
sentences.zh: “哇，我们不再关押那么多年轻人了”，他们的第一反应可能是：

sentences.en: Well, didn't crime go up?
sentences.zh: “嗯，犯罪率没上升吗？”

sentences.en: And the reality is that crime actually declined during this period just as rapidly as the incarceration rate.
sentences.zh: 事实是，在此期间犯罪率实际上与监禁率下降得一样快。

sentences.en: So I called up my editor at the magazine and I said,
sentences.zh: 所以我给杂志社的编辑打了电话，我说：

sentences.en: How is this possible?
sentences.zh: “这怎么可能？”

sentences.en: And how is it possible that everyone is not talking about it?
sentences.zh: “为什么大家都不谈论这件事？”

sentences.en: I went on a quest to find the answers.
sentences.zh: 我开始寻找答案。

sentences.en: And you'll hear about them in this week's Sunday read.
sentences.zh: 你将在本周的“周日阅读”中听到这些内容。

sentences.en: It's an article I wrote for the magazine and what really stood out to me is this.
sentences.zh: 这是我为杂志写的一篇文章，真正让我印象深刻的是这一点。

sentences.en: We know that even a month or two behind bars has terrible consequences for teenagers.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，即使是一两个月的监禁对青少年来说也会产生可怕的后果。

sentences.en: I mean, the first juvenile prison that I ever went to as a public defender, it brought me to tears.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我作为公设辩护人去过的第一所少年监狱，让我流下了眼泪。

sentences.en: It was so isolated and barren and desolate.
sentences.zh: 它太孤立、荒凉且凄凉了。

sentences.en: I mean, it's hard to fathom what it's like to be 14 or 15 and locked up in a cell to day after day be robbed of your human potential.
sentences.zh: 我是说，很难想象一个14或15岁的孩子被关在牢房里，日复一日地被剥夺人类潜能是什么感觉。

sentences.en: Incarceration makes it less likely that a kid will ever graduate from high school and more likely that they'll be arrested as an adult.
sentences.zh: 监禁使得孩子从高中毕业的可能性降低，而成年后被捕的可能性增加。

sentences.en: And what we've seen over the past 20 years is this radical experiment of not locking up kids for offenses, especially drug offenses, where prison was once routine.
sentences.zh: 在过去的20年里，我们看到了一场激进的实验，即不再因犯罪（尤其是毒品犯罪）而关押孩子，而曾经这些罪行通常会被判入狱。

sentences.en: Just putting them directly in an alternative to incarceration, such as counseling or an education or job training program.
sentences.zh: 而是直接让他们接受监禁的替代方案，例如咨询、教育或职业培训项目。

sentences.en: We now have a slew of research-backed options that are working and crime is dropping.
sentences.zh: 我们现在有大量基于研究的有效方案，犯罪率正在下降。

sentences.en: In fact, locking up fewer young people might even be part of why youth crime has declined.
sentences.zh: 事实上，减少关押年轻人甚至可能是青少年犯罪率下降的原因之一。
